compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX5090 (Blackwell, sm_120): high HBM/GDDR7 BW (~1.8TB/s), large L2, abundant SMs, strong fp16 tensor cores. Problem size: N=1, Cin=16, Cout=32, H=720, W=1280. Conv3x3 fp16 with 16->32 ch is small enough that whole filter (32*16*9 = 4608 halves = 9KB) easily fits in shared memory or registers.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Pipeline: Conv2d(3x3,pad=1,16->32) + ReLU + AvgPool2x2 on 1x16x720x1280 fp16. Output: 1x32x360x640. Conv FLOPs ~ 2*16*32*9*720*1280 ≈ 8.5 GFLOPs (small). Memory: input 28.8MB, output (post pool) 14.7MB. Likely memory-bound for input streaming; full fusion (conv+relu+avgpool) eliminates intermediate 29.5MB write/read.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Need to ensure tensor-core or vectorized fp16 math; avoid scalar __half2float bottleneck.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Dominant cost is reading input (1*16*720*1280*2=29.5MB) and writing pooled output (14.7MB). Without fusion, intermediate conv output (1*32*720*1280*2=59MB) doubles traffic. Full fusion is the biggest win.
memory_bandwidth.risk: If we don't fuse pool with conv, BW wasted on 59MB intermediate.

register_pressure.notes: Weights are tiny (9KB); easily fits in shared memory. Per-thread accumulators for Cout=32 outputs over 2x2 pool window manageable.
register_pressure.risk: If a thread computes all 32 output channels for a 2x2 tile, ~128 fp32 accumulators — borderline but viable.

nodes.notes:
ANALYSIS:
1) Classification: stencil (3x3 conv) + elementwise (ReLU) + reduction-like (2x2 avgpool). Dense, fixed small channel dims (Cin=16, Cout=32), large spatial (720x1280), N=1, fp16.
2) Math: out[co,oh,ow] = avg over 2x2 of ReLU(bias[co] + sum_{ci,kh,kw} in[ci,2oh+kh-1+dh,2ow+kw-1+dw] * w[co,ci,kh,kw]). Reductions over Cin,kh,kw and 2x2 pool. All output elements independent.
3) Layout: NCHW contiguous fp16. Input read with 3x3 overlap (high reuse along H,W). Weights tiny (9KB), read-once-per-block. Output written once.
4) Regimes: (a) memory-bound streaming of input/output (current main cost), (b) compute-bound if we tile aggressively with tensor cores, (c) launch/latency-bound for tiny work — not this case (large spatial).
5) Knobs: tile shape in HxW, channel parallelism (Cout per thread/block), shared-mem staging of input halo & weights, vectorized half2/uint4 loads, fp16 vs fp32 accumulators, fused vs split kernels, WMMA tensor cores.
6) Skeleton: one fused kernel — each block produces a tile of pooled outputs (e.g., 8x16 pooled = 16x32 conv) for all 32 output channels; load input halo (Cin slices) + 2x2-strided neighborhood into shared memory; load weights into shared/constant memory; each thread accumulates partial sums across Cin/kh/kw using half2 FMA; apply ReLU; reduce 2x2 pool; write output. Single sync between halo load and compute.
7) Families:
  - F1 (TOP, full-fusion): single kernel, shared-mem tiled conv+relu+avgpool. Avoids 59MB intermediate. Working set fits easily.
  - F2: tensor-core (WMMA/mma.sync) im2col-in-shared fused with pool. Higher compute throughput but conv is small and likely BW-bound; complexity high.
  - F3: split fused (conv+relu) and (avgpool) custom kernels, vectorized half2. Easier but loses fusion benefit.
Forbidden tactic-named families avoided.
Initial open actions below propose F1 variants and a quick win.

action.description: Write a single fused CUDA kernel that performs Conv3x3+bias+ReLU+AvgPool2x2 in one pass. Each block produces a tile of pooled outputs covering all 32 output channels. Stage the 3x3 input halo for the corresponding conv region in shared memory (one Cin channel at a time or all 16 at once — 16*tile_h*tile_w*2B fits). Keep weights (9KB) in shared memory loaded once. Use fp32 accumulators per (co, pooled_h, pooled_w). After conv+bias+ReLU, reduce 2x2 within registers and write half output. Eliminates the 59MB intermediate tensor entirely.
action.rationale: Reference does separate conv (writes 59MB) + pool (re-reads 59MB). Fusion removes that round trip; with tiny weights and high reuse, a single tiled kernel should be strongly memory-bound on input only (~30MB read + 15MB write).
action.title: Fully fused Conv+ReLU+AvgPool single kernel (tiled, shared-mem)

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX5090 SMs ~170; tile 16x32 conv output per block → ~720*1280/4/(8*16) ≈ 1800 blocks — plenty of parallelism. Shared mem per block: 16*18*34*2 ≈ 19KB input halo + 9KB weights ≈ 28KB, fits.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Compute throughput 78.6%, math pipe throttle is top stall — FFMA bound on per-thread 16-output inner loop. Tensor cores unused.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Achieved 28.8 GB/s, mem throughput only 5% — well below DRAM peak. Fusion eliminated intermediate. L2 hit 69% suggests good reuse.

register_pressure.notes: 40 regs/thread, 19584 B smem, occupancy 62%. Room to push occupancy if regs drop.

nodes.notes: CURRENT: does=single fused kernel computing Conv3x3+bias+ReLU+AvgPool2x2 with weights in constant mem, input tile in smem, 16 pooled outputs per thread. bottleneck=compute (math pipe throttle 2.5%, compute_tp 78.6%, mem_tp 5%). FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent=yes. UPDATE_BELIEF: 5.91x speedup confirms fusion thesis; now compute-bound on FFMA, not memory. next bet: reduce FFMA cost via half2 SIMD or WMMA (m16n16k16 fits Cout=32,Cin=16 perfectly); or improve occupancy by lowering registers / increasing parallelism. PERF_GAP: expected 4.0x, observed 5.91x — better than predicted because L2 reuse across blocks higher than assumed.

action.description: Keep the two-kernel structure but heavily optimize each: (1) Conv+ReLU: each thread computes multiple output channels for one spatial pixel using half2 vectorization across Cin (pairs); cache weights in shared/constant; use __ldg for inputs. (2) AvgPool: vectorize 2x2 with uint4 loads (8 halves at once) so each thread pools 4 output pixels. Easier to implement than full fusion, but keeps intermediate traffic.
action.rationale: Quick baseline improvement; isolates which kernel dominates. Useful as a safety net if full fusion has bugs.
action.title: Vectorized split kernels (conv+relu, then avgpool)

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: half2 FMA doubles fp16 throughput; constant memory for 9KB weights ideal.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Conv kernel reuses input only via L1/L2 not shared — leaves perf on table.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: L2 reuse insufficient for 3x3 overlap; may still be BW-bound on intermediate.

register_pressure.notes: Low; each thread holds few accumulators.

nodes.notes: DEPRIORITIZED: dominated by n1b 16.78x. Splitting reintroduces global intermediates and loses fusion locality.

action.description: Implement the conv inner loop using WMMA fragments (16x16x16 fp16) by treating each 2x2 pool tile as a small GEMM in shared memory (im2col-in-shared for a tile). After WMMA accumulate, apply bias+ReLU+2x2 reduction and write pooled output. Targets the Blackwell tensor cores for maximal compute throughput while still fusing the pool.
action.rationale: Tensor cores can crush the 8.5 GFLOP conv workload, leaving only input/output BW. Combined with fused pool gives best of both worlds — but high implementation risk.
action.title: Tensor-core (WMMA) fused conv+relu+avgpool

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: WMMA requires M,N,K multiples of 16. Cin=16, Cout=32 fit naturally. Im2col tile in shared memory needed.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Best compute density; problem may not need it since likely BW-bound.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Complexity, layout fiddling, correctness with halo padding.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Same as full fusion path on BW; compute throughput far in excess of need.
memory_bandwidth.risk: BW likely still the limiter — diminishing returns vs n1.

action.description: Profile/sanity check: keep reference structure but only fuse the AvgPool2x2 into the conv kernel's tail (each thread that computes a conv pixel also contributes via atomic/shared reduction to its pooled output). This is a stepping stone toward n1 without full tiling.
action.rationale: Diagnostic — measures the value of eliminating the intermediate even without tiling. Lower ceiling than n1.

kernel_summary: Fused Conv2d(3x3, pad=1, 16->32) + ReLU + AvgPool2d(2x2) on a single 1x16x720x1280 fp16 tensor on RTX5090. Total conv work is small (~8.5 GFLOPs) and weights are tiny (9KB), so the workload is fundamentally memory-bandwidth bound on the input (29.5MB) and output (14.7MB). The reference splits the pipeline into two kernels, materializing a 59MB intermediate — eliminating that round-trip via full single-kernel fusion is the dominant optimization. Constraints: fp16 NCHW contiguous, tolerance rtol=atol=0.01, must expose set_params, output shape 1x32x360x640.
open_questions: Does the evaluator measure end-to-end (compile + first run) or steady-state? Affects whether autotuning is worthwhile.
Is N always 1, or can batch vary? Current grid sizing assumes N=1; need to confirm get_inputs is the only shape.
What's the reference kernel's measured latency on RTX5090 so we can target a concrete speedup?
Are fp16 accumulators acceptable within rtol=0.01, or do we need fp32 accumulation for the 16*9=144 sum?
Is bias always present (Conv2d default bias=True is set), so we can hardcode the bias path?
Is cuDNN available/used inside the reference's 'simple' kernel? The reference comment says cuDNN/ATen but the .cu shows a naive kernel — confirms reference is the naive kernel (good — easy to beat).
Does RTX5090 (sm_120) WMMA support fp16x fp16 -> fp32 at 16x16x16 as on sm_80+? Needed before committing to n3.
What's the optimal shared-memory tile size considering 228KB shared/SM on Blackwell vs occupancy targets?
